faqs.q: How much does a Spanish Water Dog cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $800–$3,000 for a Spanish Water Dog puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Spanish Water Dog?
faqs.a: Budget $150–$300 per month for a Spanish Water Dog, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Mid-size breeds sit in the moderate cost range across most ownership categories.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Spanish Water Dog?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($500–900), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming adds $400–$1,200 annually for Spanish Water Dogs due to their coat type.

faqs.q: How much does a Spanish Water Dog cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Spanish Water Dog are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,000–$4,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Spanish Water Dog?
faqs.a: Spanish Water Dogs need brushing 3–4 times per week to prevent matting.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Spanish Water Dogs shed a lot?
faqs.a: Spanish Water Dogs shed minimally. A weekly brush is usually sufficient.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Spanish Water Dog need?
faqs.a: A wide-tooth comb, pin brush, and detangling spray are the core tools for a Spanish Water Dog's curly coat. Add a nail grinder and ear cleaner for complete at-home maintenance.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Spanish Water Dog?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Spanish Water Dogs that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Spanish Water Dogs easy to train?
faqs.a: Spanish Water Dogs are considered easier to train than average — they respond quickly to reward-based methods and generalise cues well. Short 10–15 minute sessions outperform long correction-heavy drills.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Spanish Water Dog?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Spanish Water Dogs. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Spanish Water Dog?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Spanish Water Dog?
faqs.a: Most Spanish Water Dogs learn basic obedience cues (sit, stay, come, down) within 2–4 weeks of daily practice. Reliable recall in distracting environments typically takes 2–3 months of consistent reinforcement.

faqs.q: What health problems do Spanish Water Dogs commonly have?
faqs.a: Spanish Water Dogs are most commonly associated with hip dysplasia. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Spanish Water Dogs live?
faqs.a: Spanish Water Dogs have an average lifespan of 12–14 years. Good nutrition, appropriate exercise, weight management and regular vet visits are the key factors in achieving the upper end of this range.

faqs.q: Are Spanish Water Dogs prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Spanish Water Dogs have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Spanish Water Dog puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Spanish Water Dog puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Spanish Water Dog-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Spanish Water Dogs good with kids?
faqs.a: Spanish Water Dogs can do well with children when properly socialised from puppyhood. Every dog is an individual — early exposure to children's behaviour (noise, sudden movements) is the most effective preparation.

faqs.q: Do Spanish Water Dogs get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Spanish Water Dogs are generally sociable with other dogs, particularly when well-socialised from puppyhood. Introduce new dogs on neutral territory and keep initial meetings brief and positive.

faqs.q: Do Spanish Water Dogs bark a lot?
faqs.a: Spanish Water Dogs tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Spanish Water Dogs good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Spanish Water Dogs can live in apartments if their exercise needs are met consistently. The key variable is owner commitment to daily walks and enrichment — breed size alone doesn't determine apartment suitability.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Spanish Water Dog need per day?
faqs.a: Spanish Water Dogs need approximately 60–90 minutes of exercise daily. Split across at least two sessions daily, with one higher-intensity session (running, fetch, swimming) and one loose-lead sniff walk. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Spanish Water Dogs good running partners?
faqs.a: Yes — Spanish Water Dogs make excellent running partners once fully grown (typically 12–18 months for medium breeds, 18–24 months for large breeds). Start with shorter distances and build gradually to protect developing joints.

faqs.q: What happens if a Spanish Water Dog doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Under-exercised Spanish Water Dogs often develop destructive behaviours — chewing, digging, excessive barking, and hyperactivity indoors. These are symptoms of frustration, not bad temperament. Two missed exercise sessions back-to-back typically shows up as restlessness or nuisance behaviour.

faqs.q: Can a Spanish Water Dog be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Spanish Water Dog depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A standard 20-foot long-line gives freedom while maintaining safety during the training phase.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Spanish Water Dog?
faqs.a: A Spanish Water Dog needs approximately 1½–3 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Spanish Water Dog?
faqs.a: Adult Spanish Water Dogs should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Spanish Water Dog?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Active Spanish Water Dogs benefit from higher-protein formulas (26–30% crude protein) to support muscle maintenance.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Spanish Water Dog from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Most Spanish Water Dogs can transition to adult food between 12 and 15 months. Transition gradually over 7–10 days — mix 25% new food with 75% old food and shift the ratio every 2 days to avoid digestive upset.

faqs.q: Is a Spanish Water Dog a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Spanish Water Dogs are manageable for motivated first-time owners who research the breed, commit to early training, and have realistic expectations about time and cost.

faqs.q: Are Spanish Water Dogs good family dogs?
faqs.a: Spanish Water Dogs can be excellent family dogs for active households. They thrive with children who can match their energy level. A calm household with limited exercise may not suit this breed's temperament.

faqs.q: Do Spanish Water Dogs do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Spanish Water Dogs form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Spanish Water Dog?
faqs.a: Plan for 2–3 hours per day dedicated to your Spanish Water Dog — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction. Add 15–30 minutes for grooming 3–4 times weekly. The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
